Package setup

Source: vignettes/pkg_setup.Rmd
pkg_setup.Rmd

Introduction

This vignette contains code and annotations to create a package. This code is needed only once to set up a package from scratch. Further package development is described in the vignette Package development: utils::vignette("pkg_devel", package = "develcoder").

Check existing packages

To search for functionality in existing packages, see the pointers given at the CRAN task view Package Development, the search page of R-universe which is also available with AI-assisted extended search capabilities, and packages pkgmatch and pkgsearch. Section R packages in the vignette R packages from package checkrpkgs gives an overview of repositories containing R packages: utils::vignette("r_pkgs", package = "checkrpkgs").

Choose a name 

pkgname <- "mypkgname"

# Is the intended name valid?
pkgname_valid <- pkgdepends::is_valid_package_name(nm = pkgname)
if(!pkgname_valid) {
  stop("Package name ", progutils::paste_quoted(pkgname), " is not valid: ",
       attr(pkgname_valid, which = "reason"))
}

# Is the intended name available?
unlist(pkgdepends::pkg_name_check(name = pkgname)$basics)
utils::browseURL(url = paste0("https://github.com/search?q=", pkgname,
                              "&type=repositories"))
utils::browseURL(url = paste0("https://github.com/search?q=", pkgname,
                              "+language%3AR+&type=repositories"))

Create the package

The code below creates the package through usethis::create_package(). See the usethis vignette usethis setup and help("use_description", package = "usethis") for details.

usethis::create_package() uses information stored in .Rprofile files to fill in default information. Such files can exist in various locations, for example at D:\Userdata\<username>\Documents\.Rprofile: use usethis::edit_r_profile() to open the .Rprofile file that usethis finds, see help("Startup") for details.

path_to_package <- file.path(getwd(), pkgname)
path_to_package
usethis::create_package(path = path_to_package)
desc::desc() # show contents of the DESCRIPTION file

Do:

  • Update the Title field of the DESCRIPTION file
  • Update the Description field of the DESCRIPTION file
  • Check if the automatically filled in information is correct

Add package-wide documentation

License

A license file makes clear what use of your package is allowed. Overviews of licenses are available at various websites:

  • Blue oak council
  • choosealicense
  • CreativeCommons
  • ELRA License Wizard
  • GNU.org
  • Licensing Assistant
  • Open Source Initiative
  • SPDX license list
  • System Package Data Exchange
  • tl;drLegal

Some legal details are provided at The Legal Side of Open Source.

CRAN only allows packages with licences from this list. See the section ‘Licences’ in help("library") on how to notify users that a package uses a license that is not-known-to-be-Free or Open Source Software.

usethis provides utility functions to add licenses (see help("licenses", package = "usethis"). For example, to add a MIT license:

usethis::use_mit_license()

Citation

A citation file makes clear how your package should be cited. See the documentation in the R package cffr and the GitHub page Citation file format for details on the ‘Citation File Format’ used here, and help("citation", package = "utils") on the base R citation style.

cffr::cff_write(dependencies = FALSE)

README 

usethis::use_readme_rmd()

Do:

  • Manually update README.Rmd
    • Add a badge with the version number by including the following code in the README.Rmd file (the badge does not work if the GitHub repository is private):
      ![](https://img.shields.io/github/r-package/v/<repository>/<pkg>?color=blue)
    • See the file README_template.Rmd in the folder inst/templates for pointers on useful content.
    • Knit the README.Rmd file to produce a README.md file.

Troubleshooting

The usethis practice of using devtools::build_readme() to update README.md requires that README.Rmd and README.md are staged at the same time. To remove this requirement, delete the hidden file .git/hooks/pre-commit from the R project folder, see the section ‘Description’ in help("use_readme_rmd", package = "usethis") for details.

Package overview

A package overview through the file R/<pkg>-package.R makes that, if package <pkg> has been loaded (i.e., library(<pkg>) has been run), help("<pkg>") produces a relevant description of the package with links to GitHub and to the package website. It is also used by usethis to list imported functions, and can be configured to give an overview of the functions in the package.

usethis::use_package_doc() # Create R/<pkg>-package.R

NEWS 

usethis::use_news_md() # Create NEWS.md

Set up testing infrastructure

It is convenient to have a collection of tests for your functions (see section Add tests in vignette Package development for background. Various packages can be used to create and run such tests, see section Packages tests from the CRAN Task View Package Development and Maintenance for an overview. To use package tinytest for testing, set up its infrastructure through:

tinytest::setup_tinytest(pkgdir = ".")
devtools::document()

To use package testthat for testing, set up its infrastructure through:

usethis::use_test("<func>")
devtools::document()

Set up a GitHub repository

For more information about setting up and using GitHub and Git, see the vignette Using Git and GitHub from package checkrpkgs: utils::vignette("git_github", package = "checkrpkgs").

usethis::use_git(message = "Initial commit")
# Notes:
# - If you get the error message 'You are not the current owner of the
#   GitHub repository', restart R as administrator and try again.
# - You might need to refresh the browser after the GitHub repository is created.
usethis::use_github(private = TRUE)
usethis::git_vaccinate()

The code below can be used to change the name of the default branch of the current repository from master to main, see the blogpost from Posit for details.

usethis::git_default_branch() # show default branch for the current repository
usethis::git_default_branch_rename(from = "master", to = "main")
# Sometimes this takes a while before it works
usethis::git_default_branch_rediscover()

Automate checks

GitHub Actions (GHA) is a continuous integration service to automatically run code upon certain triggers. These triggers are defined in workflows, see the reference and the How-to. The workflow check-standard.yaml from r-lib runs R CMD check for the latest version of R on Linux, MacOS and Windows, as well as the previous and development version of R on Linux. The workflow check-no-suggests.yaml checks that the code passes R CMD check even if dependencies in Suggests are not installed.

usethis::use_github_action("check-standard")
usethis::use_github_action("check-no-suggests")

After setting up these workflows, adjust the created .yaml files (i.e., <pkg>\.github\workflows\check-standard.yaml and <pkg>\.github\workflows\check-no-suggests.yaml) to include some other useful triggers for GitHub Actions (see the template files check-standard.yaml and check-no-suggests.yaml in folder templates in the local package folder or in inst/templates on the GitHub repository):

  • you made changes, or someone else proposed changes to code in the current repository:
    add pull_request: to section on: to run GitHub Actions on pull requests. You can remove push from section on:: it should be sufficient to run R CMD check locally before pushing and run GitHub Actions on pull requests.
  • you made changes to a repository and want to check if a reverse dependency (i.e., a package that depends on the package you changed) is still working fine:
    add workflow_dispatch: to section on: in the .yaml file of the reverse dependency to be able to manually trigger GitHub Actions. See section Use GitHub Actions in the vignette Package development how to use it: utils::vignette("pkg_devel", package = "develcoder").
  • someone else made changes to packages your package depends on:
    add schedule: - cron: "23 4 * * 6" to section on: to run every Saturday on 04:23 UTC. The cron specification consists of five elements that indicate the minute (0 - 59), hour (0 - 23), day of the month (1 - 31), month (1 - 12), and day of the week (0 - 6). This timing is approximate and the actual time the check is run depends on how busy the servers are.
  • If the package declares a dependency on a minimum R version in its DESCRIPTION file, it is useful to specify that minimum declared R version to run in addition to the default ones used in the template: for example,
    add - {os: ubuntu-latest, r: '4.1.0'} to section matrix: config: to also run the workflow with R version 4.1.0 if your package declares R 4.1.0 as minimum version.

For further documentation, see the section GHA: documentation and help in the vignette Package development: utils::vignette("pkg_devel", package = "develcoder").

Set up a package website

Package websites make it possible for people to look at your package without installing it. The package website also automatically creates hyperlinked cross-references to functions and documentation you refer to.

To set up a package website, you can use usethis::use_pkgdown(), see the documentation about package pkgdown and the chapter Website from the R packages book for further details.

To also set up a GitHub action to automatically build and update the package website if you push changes to your package to GitHub (defined in the file <pkg>\.github\workflows\pkgdown.yaml), run the following code:

# calls usethis::use_pkgdown() and creates '<pkg>\.github\workflows\pkgdown.yaml'
usethis::use_pkgdown_github_pages()
devtools::document() # To update package-wide documentation

After a few minutes, the website should be present. The URL has the structure https://<username>.github.io/<repository>/, e.g., https://jessealderliesten.github.io/develcoder/.

Refer from the README to the pkgdown website.

To add a light-switch to the pkgdown-website, add the line
light-switch: true below the template heading in the _pkgdown.YML file, see the documentation and the example code for this repository. The _pkgdown.YML file is located in the top-level package folder or in folder pkgdown and can also have extension .YAML; it is not the file <pkg>\.github\workflows\pkgdown.yaml that defines the GitHub Action to automatically build and update the package website if you push changes to your package to GitHub.

Documentation and further development

Further package development is described in the vignette Package development: utils::vignette("pkg_devel", package = "develcoder"). Section Documentation and help from that vignette contains further references.
